Bots got popular, and some members create far too many of them:

> As an administrator, I want to cap how many bots each member can have.

The account settings page (`/account/edit`) gets a new setting for administrators:

- "Bots per member" (a number, 5 by default)

Rules:

- A member can have at most that many bots. Deleted bots don't count.
- Administrators are not limited.
- At the limit, the bots page doesn't offer "Add a chat bot" and tells the member they've "reached the limit". Any other attempt to create a bot is refused, too.
- Lowering the limit never removes existing bots; it only blocks new ones.

Unlike human users, bots no longer join `Rooms::Open` by default. - When `add_to_all_open_rooms` is enabled on create or update, `User::Bot#sync_open_room_memberships` grants membership to all existing `Rooms::Open` (skipping rooms the bot already belongs to). `Rooms::Open#grant_access_to_all_users` grants access to `User.open_room_members` (`User.active.without_bots` plus `User.bots.where(add_to_all_open_rooms: true)`). Disabling `add_to_all_open_rooms` preserves existing memberships. - Deleting a bot calls `User#deactivate`, which sets `status: :deactivated`, clears `bot_token: nil`, `webhook_url: nil`, `add_to_all_open_rooms: false`, and removes non-direct memberships while preserving previously posted messages. - Human-only flows (`SessionsController`, `Sessions::TransfersController`, `AccountsController`, `Accounts::UsersController`, `Users::SidebarsController`) scope with `User.without_bots`. ## UI Routes & Access Control - `/account/edit` exposes the "Set up chat bots" link (`/bots`) to all signed-in members. - `BotsController` (`/bots`, `/bots/new`, `/bots/:id/edit`) lists `Current.user.created_bots.active` for members and all `User.bots` for administrators on a single unpaginated page. - Bot forms (`app/views/bots/_form.html.erb`) expose `"Name the bot"`, optional `"Webhook URL"`, and the `"Add to all open rooms"` checkbox switch (off by default). - `edit`, `update`, and `destroy` require `Current.user.can_administer?(@bot)` (creator or administrator). ## HTTP Message API - `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_token/messages` (`Bots::MessagesController#create`) authenticates via `User.find_by_bot_token` and scopes the room to `@bot.rooms`. - For non-multipart requests, `Bots::MessagesController#process_action` sets `request.request_parameters = {}` before `super` so Rails/Rack never attempts to form-parse or JSON-parse raw text bodies (e.g. `curl -d "100% done"`). - Raw bodies are UTF-8 normalized, HTML-escaped, and newline-converted before saving as ActionText `Message` bodies; `multipart/form-data` requests with `attachment` use `create_with_attachment!`. - Responses: `201 Created` (`Location: /messages/:message_id`), `422 Unprocessable Content`, `404 Not Found`, `401 Unauthorized`. ## Outgoing Webhooks & Synchronous/Async Replies - `users.webhook_url` (optional string) is normalized (`strip.presence`), validated as an `http`/`https` URL when present, and cleared alongside `bot_token` on `User#deactivate`. - `Message::Mentionee#mentioned_bots` selects active bots that are members of the room (excluding `message.creator`) referenced in ActionText mention attachments. - `Room#receive(message)` enqueues `User::Bot::WebhookJob` (`event: "mention"`) per mentioned bot with a `webhook_url`. - Whenever a bot with a `webhook_url` is newly added to a non-direct room (`Rooms::Open` or `Rooms::Closed`)—whether via `Room#memberships.grant_to`, `Membership.create!`, `Rooms::Open` creation/conversion, or `add_to_all_open_rooms`—`Room#deliver_joined_webhooks_later` / `User::Bot#deliver_joined_webhook_later` enqueues `User::Bot::WebhookJob` (`event: "joined"`) once per newly added `(bot, room)` pair. `Rooms::Direct` never triggers `joined`. - `User::Bot::WebhookJob` uses `enqueue_after_transaction_commit = true` so workers only run after memberships and rooms are committed. - `User::Bot::Webhook` POSTs `Content-Type: application/json` for `mention` (`event`, `author`, `room`, `message`) and `joined` (`event: "joined"`, `room: { id, name, reply_to }`). - Synchronous `200` responses with `Content-Type: text/plain` (HTML-escaped with `
` newlines) or `text/html` create and broadcast a reply message from the bot; `204` or non-matching responses post nothing. " }

module ApplicationHelper
  def page_title_tag
    tag.title @page_title || "Campfire"
  end

  def current_user_meta_tags
    unless Current.user.nil?
      safe_join [
        tag(:meta, name: "current-user-id", content: Current.user.id),
        tag(:meta, name: "current-user-name", content: Current.user.name)
      ]
    end
  end

  def custom_styles_tag
    if custom_styles = Current.account&.custom_styles
      tag.style(custom_styles.to_s.html_safe, data: { turbo_track: "reload" })
    end
  end

  def body_classes
    [ @body_class, admin_body_class, account_logo_body_class ].compact.join(" ")
  end

  def link_back
    back_url = request.referrer
    back_url = root_path if back_url.nil? || back_url == request.url
    link_back_to back_url
  end

  def link_back_to(destination)
    link_to destination, class: "btn" do
      image_tag("arrow-left.svg", aria: { hidden: "true" }, size: 20) +
      tag.span("Go Back", class: "for-screen-reader")
    end
  end

  private
    def admin_body_class
      "admin" if Current.user&.can_administer?
    end

    def account_logo_body_class
      "account-has-logo" if Current.account&.logo&.attached?
    end
end

Now, if `AccountsController#update` calls `@account.update!(account_params)` versus `if @account.update(account_params)`:

Should the controller rescue the error, render `:edit` with status `:unprocessable_content` (422), or simply redirect with an alert?

Let's look at `AccountsController#update` now:

def update
  @account.update!(account_params)
  redirect_to edit_account_url, notice: "✓"
end

So, adding a validation on the `Account` model for `bots_per_member` (non-nil, and greater or equal to zero) is the right approach. **Analyzing Form Patterns for "Bots per member"**

Okay, so I'm looking at the account edit page and need to figure out the best way to integrate a "Bots per member" input. I'm focusing on the current patterns: the account name and the "restrict room creation" switch. The account name uses a form with `data: { controller: "form" }`, `keydown.enter->form#submit`, and a submit button. The switch uses `change->form#submit`.

My initial thought is to put the number input for "Bots per member" in either its own form or inside the existing settings box. The primary concern is user experience and how a user will interact with the form, as well as how a test will interact with the form.

The potential issues I'm identifying:

1.  **Duplicate Save Buttons**: If I put "Bots per member" in its own form *with* a submit button, and that button's text is "Save changes" like the account name, I'll have two buttons with the same text on the page! That's a testability nightmare in Capybara or Playwright, since a test `click_button("Save changes")` is ambiguous. If I use "Save bots per member", a test looking for "Save" or "Save changes" might not work!
2.  **Auto-Submission Timing**: If I use `change->form#submit` on the number input, what happens with a browser test? Does a change trigger `input` and `change` events? If Playwright's `.fill()` triggers `change` immediately, the form will submit before the test clicks a submit button! This could cause problems if the page reloads during the click.

My current train of thought:

*   I need to consider all the cases: filling in the number input and clicking "Save changes", filling in and pressing Enter, or simply filling in and expecting it to auto-save.
*   I'm now thinking I need to find all settings inputs and how they are handled, and how tests interact with them, to understand this current design, and test design, across Campfire.

messages.content: Let's inspect `app/views/users/profiles/show.html.erb` and `app/views/accounts/custom_styles/edit.html.erb` to see how settings pages and save buttons are structured in Campfire.
messages.thinking: **Analyzing the 'Bots per Member' Setting on the Account Edit Page** Okay, I need to thoroughly consider how to implement the "Bots per member" setting on the `/account/edit` page, particularly in relation to the existing UI elements and QA testing scenarios. The goal is to provide a user-friendly and testable interface, and avoid regressions. My initial thought is to place the setting within a shaded box, similar to the "Must be admin to create new rooms" setting. I'll need to carefully examine the existing structure of `app/views/accounts/edit.html.erb`, specifically lines 52-90, to understand how forms and submission behaviors are handled. The key is to match the patterns used for the account name input (with a "Save changes" button) and the administrator toggle (autosubmits on change). I must consider the following: * **Form Structure:** Where does the form element go? Is it its own form element or inside an existing one? Based on previous structure, it seems each setting is its own form. * **Submission Behavior:** How will changes be saved? Should it auto-submit on blur/Enter (like the account name), or should it have a dedicated "Save" button? If the form autosubmits, it makes the most sense. * **QA Test Compatibility:** How will this design affect the auto-tests? * Do I need a "Save" button? If so, what should the text be to avoid ambiguity? ("Save changes" is already in use). * Will auto-tests click "Save" *or* press Enter/blur? * What happens if the test *does* click "Save" and the setting auto-submits? * Will `change->form#submit` behave like all other switches/file inputs in Campfire? To ensure testability and prevent potential issues, I must consider how auto-tests will interact with the "Bots per member" setting: * If the user *presses Enter* or blurs, does it auto-submit? * If the user clicks "Save," does it also work? My current inclination is to include both the `change->form#submit` and a submit button with `span class="for-screen-reader">Save` (NOT `"Save changes"`, so it doesn't collide with `"Save changes"` on the account name form, as it causes ambiguity). This will give QA engineers maximum flexibility in their automated tests, accommodating both keyboard and mouse interactions.

class Rooms::ClosedsController < RoomsController
  before_action :set_room, only: %i[ show edit update ]
  before_action :ensure_can_administer, only: %i[ update ]
  before_action :remember_last_room_visited, only: :show
  before_action :force_room_type, only: %i[ edit update ]
  before_action :ensure_permission_to_create_rooms, only: %i[ new create ]

  DEFAULT_ROOM_NAME = "New room"

  def show
    redirect_to room_url(@room)
  end

  def new
    @room  = Rooms::Closed.new(name: DEFAULT_ROOM_NAME)
    @users = User.active.ordered
  end

  def create
    room = Rooms::Closed.create_for(room_params, users: grantees)

    broadcast_create_room(room)
    redirect_to room_url(room)
  end

  def edit
    selected_user_ids = @room.users.pluck(:id)
    @selected_users, @unselected_users = User.active.ordered.partition { |user| selected_user_ids.include?(user.id) }
  end

  def update
    @room.update! room_params
    @room.memberships.revise(granted: grantees, revoked: revokees)

    broadcast_update_room
    redirect_to room_url(@room)
  end

  private
    # Allows us to edit an open room and turn it into a closed one on saving.
    def force_room_type
      @room = @room.becomes!(Rooms::Closed)
    end

    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other, so both are in reach here. Direct
    # rooms never are: converting one would let its creator revise who's in it.
    def room_scope
      Current.user.rooms.without_directs
    end

    def grantees
      User.where(id: grantee_ids)
    end

    def revokees
      @room.users.where.not(id: grantee_ids)
    end

    def grantee_ids
      params.fetch(:user_ids, [])
    end

    def broadcast_create_room(room)
      each_user_and_html_for(room) do |user, html|
        broadcast_prepend_to user, :rooms, target: :shared_rooms, html: html
      end
    end

    def broadcast_update_room
      each_user_and_html_for(@room) do |user, html|
        broadcast_replace_to user, :rooms, target: [ @room, :list ], html: html
      end
    end

    def each_user_and_html_for(room)
      # Optimization to avoid rendering the same partial for every user
      html = render_to_string(partial: "users/sidebars/rooms/shared", locals: { room: room })

      room.users.each { |user| yield user, html }
    end
end

    assert_turbo_stream_broadcasts :rooms, count: 1 do

    assert_redirected_to room_url(Room.last)
  end

    assert_response :forbidden

  end

  end

**Edge Case Analysis for Bot Limits**

Okay, let's break this down systematically. We're talking about bot limits per member, and the interaction with various scenarios. First, the core database interaction is crucial: if an account has no settings or an empty settings hash initially, the default bot limit is `5`. This shouldn't be affected when updating other settings.

Next, we validate the input: what about different inputs for the `"Bots per member"` setting? Zero (`0`) and high numbers like ten (`10`) are valid and are properly saved. But when someone provides an empty string (`""`) or negative numbers (`-1`) it's rejected with a 422 error, and the previous value should remain. Additionally, non-admins should be forbidden from updating the account settings.

The key observation is this type casting issue, i.e., what happens if someone provides a string like `"2.5"` or `"abc"` in an HTTP request?  The integer casting might silently convert `"abc"` to `0`. However, the HTML `<input type="number" ...>` and Rails integer casting helps prevent these issues.

We also need to consider the UI interaction on the accounts edit page for admins vs non-admins. Admin accounts should see the bot limit setting, and non-admins shouldn't, so that's covered via authorization.

Now, let's explore scenarios for users who reach the limits. When a member reaches their bot limit, their `/bots` page accurately reflects that, listing their existing bots but blocking the `"Add a chat bot"` link, and telling the member that they've hit the limit.  Direct access to the `/bots/new` and `POST /bots` routes should result in 403 Forbidden errors.  Validation should prevent bot creation through the model, i.e., `User.create` when the limit is reached.

Crucially, deactivated (deleted) bots *do not* count towards the limit. This allows for clean bot management – members can delete bots to open up space for new ones.

Administrators are exempt from these limits. Even with a setting of `0` bots, admins can create as many bots as they need. They don't have limits.

The system is designed so that lowering the limit does not retroactively remove existing bots. Members retain their existing bots, but they are blocked from creating *new* ones until their active count falls below the new limit. They can still edit or delete existing bots, even if they're over the limit.  This editing process will function seamlessly for bots over the limit, since `ensure_under_bot_limit` and `validate_bot_limit` do not apply on updates or deletions.

We also have to consider what happens when an administrator updates a bot for a member over the limit. This should work without issue, since limit validation is only on creation.

Let's also review the error handling in the `edit.html.erb` view. The form uses `@account.settings.bots_per_member` to ensure the correct values and error messages are displayed. So we're good there. And the use of `Current.account` is fine in the settings form, given our system.

Finally, we need to update `docs/bots.md` to document the functionality, and ensure everything stays consistent for future work.

So, let's get down to writing comprehensive tests. We need to cover the account model, the user/bot model, and the account and bot controllers. I need to review existing tests first, and then add tests to fully validate the behavior in all of these edge cases.

**Avoiding Unintended Interpolation**

Right, so I just caught myself out. Classic mistake! I was using a standard `<<~RUBY` heredoc in Ruby, and, d'oh!, I realized I had this `#{new_bot_path}` variable in there, which meant the interpreter would interpolate it prematurely. The fix? Simple. Switch to a single-quoted heredoc: `<<~'RUBY'`. That keeps everything inside the heredoc as a raw string until the script actually runs. { "returncode": 0, "output": "# Omakase Ruby styling for Rails inherit_gem: { rubocop-rails-omakase: rubocop.yml } # Chat Bots Architecture ## Data Model - Bots are stored as `User` records with `role: :bot` (enum values: `member: 0, administrator: 1, bot: 2`). - `users.bot_token` stores a 24-character `SecureRandom.base58` credential (unique indexed, filtered from logs and `inspect` via `:token` in `filter_parameters`). - `users.creator_id` references the `User` who created the bot, enabling `User#can_administer?(bot)` for creators and administrators. - `users.add_to_all_open_rooms` (boolean, default `false`) controls whether a bot automatically joins open rooms. Unlike human users, bots no longer join `Rooms::Open` by default. - When `add_to_all_open_rooms` is enabled on create or update, `User::Bot#sync_open_room_memberships` grants membership to all existing `Rooms::Open` (skipping rooms the bot already belongs to). `Rooms::Open#grant_access_to_all_users` grants access to `User.open_room_members` (`User.active.without_bots` plus `User.bots.where(add_to_all_open_rooms: true)`). Disabling `add_to_all_open_rooms` preserves existing memberships. - Deleting a bot calls `User#deactivate`, which sets `status: :deactivated`, clears `bot_token: nil`, `webhook_url: nil`, `add_to_all_open_rooms: false`, and removes non-direct memberships while preserving previously posted messages. - Human-only flows (`SessionsController`, `Sessions::TransfersController`, `AccountsController`, `Accounts::UsersController`, `Users::SidebarsController`) scope with `User.without_bots`. ## UI Routes & Access Control - `/account/edit` exposes the "Set up chat bots" link (`/bots`) to all signed-in members. - `BotsController` (`/bots`, `/bots/new`, `/bots/:id/edit`) lists `Current.user.created_bots.active` for members and all `User.bots` for administrators on a single unpaginated page. - Bot forms (`app/views/bots/_form.html.erb`) expose `"Name the bot"`, optional `"Webhook URL"`, and the `"Add to all open rooms"` checkbox switch (off by default). - `edit`, `update`, and `destroy` require `Current.user.can_administer?(@bot)` (creator or administrator). ## HTTP Message API - `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_token/messages` (`Bots::MessagesController#create`) authenticates via `User.find_by_bot_token` and scopes the room to `@bot.rooms`. - For non-multipart requests, `Bots::MessagesController#process_action` sets `request.request_parameters = {}` before `super` so Rails/Rack never attempts to form-parse or JSON-parse raw text bodies (e.g. `curl -d "100% done"`). - Raw bodies are UTF-8 normalized, HTML-escaped, and newline-converted before saving as ActionText `Message` bodies; `multipart/form-data` requests with `attachment` use `create_with_attachment!`. - Responses: `201 Created` (`Location: /messages/:message_id`), `422 Unprocessable Content`, `404 Not Found`, `401 Unauthorized`. ## Outgoing Webhooks & Synchronous/Async Replies - `users.webhook_url` (optional string) is normalized (`strip.presence`), validated as an `http`/`https` URL when present, and cleared alongside `bot_token` on `User#deactivate`. - `Message::Mentionee#mentioned_bots` selects active bots that are members of the room (excluding `message.creator`) referenced in ActionText mention attachments. - `Room#receive(message)` enqueues `User::Bot::WebhookJob` (`event: "mention"`) per mentioned bot with a `webhook_url`. - Whenever a bot with a `webhook_url` is newly added to a non-direct room (`Rooms::Open` or `Rooms::Closed`)—whether via `Room#memberships.grant_to`, `Membership.create!`, `Rooms::Open` creation/conversion, or `add_to_all_open_rooms`—`Room#deliver_joined_webhooks_later` / `User::Bot#deliver_joined_webhook_later` enqueues `User::Bot::WebhookJob` (`event: "joined"`) once per newly added `(bot, room)` pair. `Rooms::Direct` never triggers `joined`. - `User::Bot::WebhookJob` uses `enqueue_after_transaction_commit = true` so workers only run after memberships and rooms are committed. - `User::Bot::Webhook` POSTs `Content-Type: application/json` for `mention` (`event`, `author`, `room`, `message`) and `joined` (`event: "joined"`, `room: { id, name, reply_to }`). - Synchronous `200` responses with `Content-Type: text/plain` (HTML-escaped with `
` newlines) or `text/html` create and broadcast a reply message from the bot; `204` or non-matching responses post nothing. " }

`multipart/form-data` requests with `attachment` use `create_with_attachment!`. - Responses: `201 Created` (`Location: /messages/:message_id`), `422 Unprocessable Content`, `404 Not Found`, `401 Unauthorized`. ## Outgoing Webhooks & Synchronous/Async Replies - `users.webhook_url` (optional string) is normalized (`strip.presence`), validated as an `http`/`https` URL when present, and cleared alongside `bot_token` on `User#deactivate`. - `Message::Mentionee#mentioned_bots` selects active bots that are members of the room (excluding `message.creator`) referenced in ActionText mention attachments. - `Room#receive(message)` enqueues `User::Bot::WebhookJob` (`event: "mention"`) per mentioned bot with a `webhook_url`. - Whenever a bot with a `webhook_url` is newly added to a non-direct room (`Rooms::Open` or `Rooms::Closed`)—whether via `Room#memberships.grant_to`, `Membership.create!`, `Rooms::Open` creation/conversion, or `add_to_all_open_rooms`—`Room#deliver_joined_webhooks_later` / `User::Bot#deliver_joined_webhook_later` enqueues `User::Bot::WebhookJob` (`event: "joined"`) once per newly added `(bot, room)` pair. `Rooms::Direct` never triggers `joined`. - `User::Bot::WebhookJob` uses `enqueue_after_transaction_commit = true` so workers only run after memberships and rooms are committed. - `User::Bot::Webhook` POSTs `Content-Type: application/json` for `mention` (`event`, `author`, `room`, `message`) and `joined` (`event: "joined"`, `room: { id, name, reply_to }`). - Synchronous `200` responses with `Content-Type: text/plain` (HTML-escaped with `
` newlines) or `text/html` create and broadcast a reply message from the bot; `204` or non-matching responses post nothing.
